claim_boundary: First-ever read of VisDrone2019-DET-test-dev (1,610 images, public GT, never used for any prior selection decision in this project). This result is reported as-is and must not be used to reverse or reselect the already-promoted highres-pilot checkpoint -- doing so would turn test-dev into another selection surface and defeat its purpose as a locked test.
interpretation: The AP-small gain that passed the pre-registered gate (+0.010 minimum) on val (+0.0223) does not clearly replicate on the locked test-dev split (+0.0027, well under the gate threshold). The overall AP gain also shrinks substantially (val +0.0325 -> test-dev +0.0144, 44% of the val-measured gain). This is consistent with the risk flagged before test-dev was sourced: repeated selection against the same 548-image val set across many experiments (checkpoint selection, mode selection, the pilot's own gate, tracker/ReID comparisons) likely inflated the apparent size of this specific gain. The promotion decision is NOT reversed by this single read (that would make test-dev another selection surface), but the practical small-object benefit of the promoted checkpoint should now be treated as unconfirmed, not established, until independently retested.
next_step: Any future small-object detection lever (copy-paste augmentation, architecture/loss retests) must be gated against this locked test-dev split directly, not against val, to avoid repeating this inflation.
